# Processes: DNA isolation, PCR, gel electrophoresis, gene transfer

## 1. Introduction
Opening frame for **Processes** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Biotechnology — Principles and Processes fill pass.

## 2. Hierarchy body — every syllabus sub-point
### Processes: DNA isolation
### PCR
### gel electrophoresis
### gene transfer

Fill order per concept: definition → structure → process → significance (§3.2). Step-by-step numbered points, Pioneer style.

The working processes of biotech: **DNA isolation** (lyse cells, remove proteins, precipitate pure DNA), **PCR** (polymerase chain reaction — amplify a DNA segment a billion-fold in hours using Taq polymerase through denaturation, primer annealing and extension cycles), **gel electrophoresis** (separate DNA fragments by size through an agarose gel — DNA is negative, so it runs to the anode), and **gene transfer** into hosts or plants.

## 3. Classified tables

Tables carry examples in every classification and characteristics row, ≤ 12 rows, and each is referenced from the body text (§3.3).

**Concept flow — the processes in the order a cloning project uses them (study in this order)**

| Step | Process | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | DNA isolation | Extract clean DNA from cells (lysis → RNase/protease → ethanol precipitation) |
| 2 | Cutting with restriction enzymes | Produce fragments with usable ends |
| 3 | PCR | Amplify the specific fragment a billion-fold |
| 4 | Gel electrophoresis | Check fragment sizes; recover the right band |
| 5 | Ligation into vector | Build the recombinant DNA |
| 6 | Gene transfer | Deliver the construct to host or plant cells |

**PCR — the three temperatures and what happens at each**

| Step | Temperature | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Denaturation | ~94–95°C | Double helix separates into two single strands |
| 2. Primer annealing | ~50–60°C | Short primers bind the flanking sequences of the target |
| 3. Extension | ~72°C | Taq polymerase builds the new strand from the primers |
| Result after n cycles | — | Target copies ≈ 2ⁿ; 30 cycles → over a billion copies |
| Why Taq polymerase | From Thermus aquaticus (hot-spring bacterium) | Survives the denaturation step — the enzyme does not need re-adding |

**Gene transfer methods — classified**

| Method | How it works | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Transformation (CaCl2 + heat shock) | Cold calcium makes membranes permeable; brief heat shock lets DNA in | Bacteria (E. coli) |
| Electroporation | Electric pulses open temporary pores | Bacteria, plant cells |
| Microinjection | DNA injected directly into the cell/nucleus with a fine needle | Animal cells, embryos |
| Biolistics (gene gun) | Gold/tungsten particles coated with DNA shot into cells | Plant cells |
| Agrobacterium tumefaciens | Disarmed Ti plasmid carries the gene into plant genome naturally | Dicot plants — nature's own genetic engineer |

## 6. Key terms and statements
Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).

**Worked example — PCR maths.** Starting with 1 copy and running 30 cycles: copies = 2³⁰ ≈ 1.07 billion. With 20 cycles: 2²⁰ ≈ 1 million. So the choice of cycle count sets sensitivity — forensic and diagnostic PCR use 30–40 cycles to detect vanishingly small starting amounts, which is also why contamination is fatal: one stray molecule becomes a billion too.

examShortTricks: Trick 1: DNA isolation: cell lysis (lysozyme/EDTA/detergent) → protease/RNase → chilled ethanol precipitation ('spooling') — the three-step order.
Trick 2: PCR three steps: denaturation 94–95 °C, primer annealing 50–60 °C, extension 72 °C (Taq polymerase) — temperatures ARE the marks; 30 cycles ≈ 10⁹ copies.
Trick 3: Gel electrophoresis: DNA moves to the anode (negative charge), smaller fragments faster; ethidium bromide + UV visualises; compare with a ladder.
Trick 4: Gene transfer: microinjection (direct into cell), gene gun (gold particles), disarmed Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium (plants) — three routes.
